How does GPS know where you are?
Your phone sends nothing to space. It only listens.
Satellites about twenty thousand kilometers up broadcast the exact time.
Radio signals travel at the speed of light.
Your phone measures how long each signal took to arrive.
Time multiplied by speed gives you distance.
One distance puts you somewhere on a giant circle.
Three circles cross at just one point.
Phone clocks are cheap, so a fourth satellite fixes the timing.
